title: Signal Type Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Signals and Systems
Continuous-Time Signals
Discrete-Time Signals
Signal Energy and Power
description: Compare continuous-time and discrete-time views of sinusoid, square wave, exponential and step signals while adjusting amplitude, frequency, phase, time shift and time scale, with closed-form energy, average power and RMS readouts.

learningObjectives: Distinguish continuous-time and discrete-time representations of the same signal
Predict how amplitude, frequency and phase change a sinusoid
Classify a signal as an energy signal or a power signal from its energy and average power
Analyze how time shifting, time scaling and time reversal change a waveform and its energy or power

assumptions: Energy, power and RMS are closed-form values for the ideal, infinitely long signal
The discrete-time view uses a fixed sampling period of 0.05 s

keyQuestions: How do power and RMS amplitude change when the amplitude doubles?
Which signal operations change the energy or power of a signal, and which do not?
Why is a decaying exponential an energy signal while a sinusoid is a power signal?
commonMisconceptions: A phase shift changes the power of a sinusoid
Compressing a signal in time leaves its energy unchanged
A discrete-time signal is defined between its samples
assessmentOpportunities: Compute the energy of 3e^(-2t)u(t) and the power of 3cos(2*pi*5t) by hand, then verify with the MicroSim
